findings.finding: Capability and local-delta receipt provenance is not an enforced graph.
findings.evidence: The receipt checks only that local_delta_receipt_ids are nonempty and unique. Evaluation never requires ThreatLocalDeltaV1.receipt_id to be in that set or to equal the referenced VisibleThreatCapabilityV1.local_delta_receipt_id. The capabilities= override is accepted without binding hashes, deck profiles, scope_version, or receipt membership to the evaluator receipt. A forged local receipt/capability pair still selected F01 A.
findings.contract: The B4 design requires an exact local-delta receipt for every candidate and exact engine/library/wrapper/card/deck provenance for every capability. A receipt for one target/deck cannot be generalized or replaced by caller-supplied metadata.
findings.required_follow_up: Bind each option fingerprint to one registered local-delta receipt, bind each capability's local_delta_receipt_id to that receipt, reject duplicate/extra/unregistered records, and compare every provenance field against an immutable fixture/config dependency manifest before scoring. Do not allow an unbound capabilities override.
findings.closure_probe: Unregistered delta -> B0_DELEGATE/UNREGISTERED_LOCAL_DELTA; direct forged capabilities override -> B0_DELEGATE/UNREGISTERED_CAPABILITIES; forged whole receipt with cap-x [0,0] -> SELECTED/B4-F01-X.
findings.residual_finding: See B4-RED-008: the evaluator validates the receipt graph and manifest shape but not a canonical content digest for the capability tuple itself.

findings.finding: B4-A treats incomplete or unqualified capability fields as facts, including arbitrary card/effect prose.
findings.evidence: VisibleThreatCapabilityV1 accepts FIXTURE_ONLY records with ready_now=None, energy_deficit=None, threat_level=None, or one missing interval endpoint unless unknown_fields happens to name the omission. damage_or_effect_semantics is only required to be a nonempty string; static prose is not rejected or bound to a qualified response receipt. B4-A checks unknown_fields but not these required-field/semantic conditions, then uses possible_level and selects. Missing ready_now, missing guaranteed_level, and 'deal 999 damage from card prose' each selected F01 A in independent probes.
findings.contract: B4-A requires every threat field needed to rank to be known and receipt-qualified. Static damage/effect prose, unqualified target/status/energy semantics, and partial capabilities must produce UNKNOWN/PARTIAL delegation, never a score.
findings.required_follow_up: Require a qualified semantic receipt and explicit known/unknown state for every field used by A; reject or delegate any missing ready/energy/threat/interval/target/status field and any non-receipt prose. Keep FIXTURE_ONLY arithmetic fixtures separate from native-qualified runtime records.
findings.closure_probe: Missing ready_now -> B0_DELEGATE/UNKNOWN_THREAT_FIELD; card prose -> B0_DELEGATE/CARD_PROSE_FORBIDDEN; hidden-like target/status/energy strings and wrong source/target ownership role -> SELECTED/B4-F01-Y.
findings.residual_finding: See B4-RED-009: semantic requirement values and source/target role are not bound to exact public option/entity contracts.

findings.finding: Lifecycle monotonicity and idempotency do not record early delegated requests.
findings.evidence: Requests are inserted into _last/_request_ids only after candidate processing selects or emits optional STOP. Delegation paths for unknown formulation, unsupported context, count/order, STOP row, duplicate semantics, incomplete coverage, and missing local deltas return before recording identity. Consequently, a supported payload changed at the same selection_seq after an unsupported request selected, and a valid lower sequence selected after a higher sequence delegated. The implementation also increments diagnostics on repeated early delegates rather than replaying a bound decision.
findings.contract: F06 requires changed/stale/out-of-order requests to reject and identical duplicates to be idempotent. State is owned by episode/player/policy and the monotonic selection identity must cover every request outcome, including B0 delegation.
findings.required_follow_up: Compute a strict request/content digest immediately after terminal-first/public validation, record every accepted request outcome before returning, reject same-identity payload changes and lower sequences after any observed request, and make duplicate delegates idempotent. Reset that identity ledger at every lifecycle boundary.
findings.closure_probe: Unknown-formulation duplicate replayed exactly; changed same-sequence payload returned STALE_OR_REUSED_REQUEST_IDENTITY; lower sequence after a higher delegated request returned STALE_OR_REUSED_REQUEST_IDENTITY; focused lifecycle/reset tests passed.

findings.finding: Fixture metadata provenance is asserted by shape, not content, and source code is the real fixture authority.
findings.evidence: materialize_b4_fixture_data only checks that fixture_metadata_sha256 is a 64-character lowercase digest; replacing the all-f value with any other digest still passes. The config declares only case IDs and the ThreatLevelScale; all public observations, capabilities, deltas, and expected behavior are hardcoded in _build_cases. There is no content hash of the canonical fixture records, source/config dependency manifest, or schema/import receipt. A caller can alter the metadata label without changing the materialized data, and source edits can change cases without a corresponding config digest failure.
findings.contract: Fixture authority and dependency/provenance integrity must be version-bound. The fixture digest must cover canonical public records, receipts, config, implementation/schema dependencies, and declared expected outcomes; a label or directory is not immutable evidence.
findings.required_follow_up: Make one declared artifact authoritative, recompute its canonical digest, bind source/config/schema/import hashes, and fail closed on any content mutation. Do not keep the case semantics solely in an un-hashed helper while treating the JSON as authority.
findings.closure_probe: In-memory metadata, dependency-manifest, and expected-outcome mutations all raised ValueError; normalized source digest independently matched the config dependency manifest.
findings.residual_finding: Direct evaluator construction with a forged whole receipt is tracked as B4-RED-008; declared config-load authority does not yet bind every runtime receipt instance.

findings.finding: NO_QUALIFIED_RESPONSE can be asserted by an unverified census flag and scores as a safe zero.
findings.evidence: When a positive option has no remaining_capability_ids and census_complete=True, the evaluator sets lower=upper=0 and selects it. current_public_fields are only nonempty strings and are not tied to a public census receipt. The independent F03 probe with arbitrary current field names and no capabilities returned SELECTED with interval (0,0).
findings.contract: The no-response sentinel is legal only after a complete qualified visible-source/capability census and target/energy/status checks. Empty or unknown capability coverage is UNKNOWN, never silently zero.
findings.required_follow_up: Require a separately registered census receipt covering the exact public snapshot, source/target scope, and all required checks; otherwise delegate with UNKNOWN_THREAT_FIELD or INCOMPLETE_THREAT_COVERAGE.
findings.closure_probe: Unregistered empty-capability census returned B0_DELEGATE/UNREGISTERED_CENSUS_RECEIPT; a registered census with matching public hash/scopes/checks/local delta selected the intended [0,0] sentinel.

findings.finding: ThreatLevelScaleV1 validation is permissive for malformed scale labels and numeric types.
findings.evidence: The constructor compares level numbers to range() using equality, so float ordinals 0.0/1.0 and bool False/1 pass. Duplicate labels also pass. from_dict coerces schema, IDs, levels, and labels with int()/str(), allowing malformed input to be normalized instead of rejected. Proper integer fixture levels and NaN/Inf capability levels are handled, and matching scale IDs are checked, but the scale schema is not strict enough for an authority shared by interval arithmetic.
findings.contract: All interval endpoints and ordinals must be finite nonnegative integers on one independently reviewed shared scale; unsupported enums and malformed provenance must fail closed rather than coerce.
findings.required_follow_up: Validate exact bool/int/string types, unique labels, immutable level mapping, and strict from_dict input without coercion; retain explicit NaN/Inf rejection tests at both scale and capability boundaries.
findings.closure_probe: Float ordinal, duplicate label, bool schema, and NaN/Inf endpoint probes all raised ValueError; corrected strict-scale tests passed.

findings.finding: The passing tests do not establish the required fresh-process and full F01-F07 qualification boundary.
findings.evidence: All eight committed B4 tests run in one pytest process. F05 permutes and mirrors only the two-option F01 case; F02-F04 and F07 receive no semantic permutation/mirror pass. There is no fresh-process test, no hidden-only mutation proof, no same-request local-delta/capability digest mutation regression, no fixture provenance mutation regression, no NaN/Inf/unsupported-enum matrix, and no separate test of each target anchor/receipt scope. The public arithmetic and basic STOP/compound cases pass, but the stage-0 design explicitly requires fresh-process boundary, complete option, provenance, permutation, mirror, lifecycle, and fail-closed review before native work.
findings.contract: B4-F01 through B4-F07 must be materialized as valid public records and independently qualified under fresh processes, semantic permutations, player mirror, hidden invariance, lifecycle/idempotency, complete options, STOP/compound, and receipt/provenance rejection.
findings.required_follow_up: Add focused regressions for every red-team finding and execute them in fresh processes across all fixture cases and both formulations. Keep the fixture verdict blocked until the complete boundary matrix is independently green.
findings.closure_probe: Fresh subprocess asserted all 11 materialized cases, original/mirror cases, both formulations and every option permutation against declared expected statuses (44 base, 72 permutation, 144 hidden/enum checks); corrected focused suite passed 18 tests.
findings.residual_finding: Capability semantic-field mutation coverage is intentionally not claimed; B4-RED-009 remains a separate blocker.

findings.finding: A forged whole B4 capability receipt with internally consistent graph and manifest is accepted without canonical capability-content binding.
findings.evidence: The corrected evaluator rejects a direct capabilities= override that differs from self.receipt, and it validates local-delta membership plus every provenance-manifest field. However, an independent probe replaced cap-x in the entire B4CapabilityReceiptV1 with the same typed capability except guaranteed_level=0 and possible_level=0. A fresh evaluator accepted that forged receipt and returned SELECTED with chosen semantic action B4-F01-X. No canonical receipt/content digest or exact capability tuple comparison is performed at evaluator construction; _validate_provenance_graph checks graph references and the fixture-shaped f... manifest, not capability semantics or levels.
findings.contract: B4 requires exact version-bound capability receipts and fixture authority. A caller cannot replace an exact visible capability's response class, source/target, requirements, or threat interval while retaining the same graph and provenance labels. Runtime scoring must consume only a canonical, content-bound receipt.
findings.required_follow_up: Bind B4CapabilityReceiptV1 to the sealed canonical fixture content/case digest, including ordered capabilities, local deltas, census receipts and expected semantics; reject any receipt whose full content is not exactly the loaded authority. Keep capabilities= overrides rejected even when a forged receipt is supplied.

findings.finding: Capability target/status/energy semantics and source/target ownership roles are not exact-qualified against the public option and visible entities.
findings.evidence: The corrected boundary catches card-prose tokens, missing ranked fields, and unresolved entity keys, but VisibleThreatCapabilityV1 accepts arbitrary nonempty target_requirements/status_constraints and any nonnegative energy tuple. The evaluator checks only that capability source/target keys exist and source_card_id matches the source entity card; it does not bind capability source/target to the current LegalOptionV1, enforce owner/zone/choice-role semantics, validate target/status/energy requirement enums, or reject hidden-like values. Independent probes changed cap-y to target_requirements=('HIDDEN_OPPONENT_HAND',), status_constraints=('opponent_deck_identity',), energy_requirements=(99,), and source=p0:s10/card=901,target=p1:s50; each still produced SELECTED/B4-F01-Y rather than B0_DELEGATE.
findings.contract: A capability is usable only when its public source entity, target entity/role, energy requirement, status constraint and legality are all known and receipt-qualified. Hidden hand/deck/Prize identity and unqualified target/status/energy semantics are UNKNOWN, not selectable facts.
findings.required_follow_up: Define strict typed/allowlisted public requirement enums; bind each capability source/target/card/attack/effect/choice role to the exact current option and visible entity owner/zone; reject hidden/private/prose-like or mismatched requirement values before interval arithmetic. Add fresh-process mutations for every semantic field and mirrored ownership case.
